title: Data Lake
description: Architecture, storage, governance, and advanced concepts for data lakes

questions.question: What is a data lake?
options: Centralized repository for raw data in native format
questions.correctAnswer: Centralized repository for raw data in native format
questions.explanation: A data lake is a centralized repository that holds raw data in its native format, supporting structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data.

questions.question: What is schema-on-read?
questions.correctAnswer: Schema applied when reading data
questions.explanation: Schema-on-read applies the schema when data is read from the lake, not when it is written, allowing flexible data ingestion.

questions.question: What is schema-on-write?
questions.correctAnswer: Schema applied when writing data
questions.explanation: Schema-on-write applies schema and data validation when data is written to the system, ensuring data consistency.

questions.question: Data lake vs warehouse - key difference?
questions.correctAnswer: Lake-raw, schema-on-read; Warehouse-structured, schema-on-write
questions.explanation: Data lakes accept data in any format with schema-on-read; data warehouses require structured data with schema-on-write.

questions.question: What is a data lakehouse?
questions.correctAnswer: Combines lake and warehouse features
questions.explanation: A data lakehouse combines the flexibility of data lakes with the reliability and performance of data warehouses.

questions.question: What is Delta Lake?
options: Open-source storage layer with ACID transactions
questions.correctAnswer: Open-source storage layer with ACID transactions
questions.explanation: Delta Lake is an open-source storage layer that brings ACID transactions to Apache Spark and big data workloads.

questions.question: What is Apache Iceberg?
options: Open table format for analytic datasets
questions.correctAnswer: Open table format for analytic datasets
questions.explanation: Apache Iceberg is an open table format for huge analytic datasets, providing reliability and simplicity.

questions.question: What is Apache Hudi?
options: Open-source data lake with upserts, deletes
questions.correctAnswer: Open-source data lake with upserts, deletes
questions.explanation: Apache Hudi provides upserts, deletes, and near-real-time ingestion capabilities to data lakes.

questions.question: What are typical data lake zones?
questions.correctAnswer: Landing, Raw, Cleaned, Curated, Consumption
questions.explanation: Typical zones are: Landing (temporary), Raw (persistent raw data), Cleaned (validated), Curated (business-ready), Consumption (optimized for users).

questions.question: What is a data swamp?
options: Disorganized data lake hard to use
questions.correctAnswer: Disorganized data lake hard to use
questions.explanation: A data swamp is what happens when a data lake lacks proper governance, metadata, and organization, making data hard to find, understand, and use.

questions.question: Which company originally developed Delta Lake?
questions.correctAnswer: Databricks
questions.explanation: Delta Lake was originally developed by Databricks as an open-source storage layer for Apache Spark.

questions.question: What file format does Delta Lake use?
questions.correctAnswer: Parquet
questions.explanation: Delta Lake uses Parquet as its underlying file format for efficient columnar storage.

questions.question: What is the Delta Lake transaction log?
options: Record of all changes made to the table
questions.correctAnswer: Record of all changes made to the table
questions.explanation: The Delta Lake transaction log is a set of JSON files that record all changes made to the table, enabling ACID transactions and time travel.

questions.question: What is time travel in Delta Lake?
options: Querying data as it was at a previous point in time
Going back in time to fix errors
questions.correctAnswer: Querying data as it was at a previous point in time
questions.explanation: Time travel in Delta Lake allows you to query data as it was at a previous version or timestamp, using the transaction log.

questions.question: What is OPTIMIZE in Delta Lake?
options: Compacts small files into larger ones
questions.correctAnswer: Compacts small files into larger ones
questions.explanation: OPTIMIZE command in Delta Lake compacts small files into larger ones to improve query performance.

questions.question: What is Z-Ordering in Delta Lake?
options: Co-locates related data for faster reads
questions.correctAnswer: Co-locates related data for faster reads
questions.explanation: Z-Ordering is a technique that co-locates related data in the same files to minimize the amount of data read during queries.

questions.question: What is VACUUM in Delta Lake?
options: Removes old files no longer referenced by the table
questions.correctAnswer: Removes old files no longer referenced by the table
questions.explanation: VACUUM removes old data files that are no longer referenced by the current table version, freeing up storage space.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the _delta_log directory?
questions.correctAnswer: Stores transaction log files
questions.explanation: The _delta_log directory stores all transaction log files that record changes to a Delta Lake table.

questions.question: Which companies originally developed Iceberg?
questions.correctAnswer: Netflix and Apple
questions.explanation: Apache Iceberg was originally developed by Netflix and Apple as an open table format.

questions.question: What is snapshot isolation in Iceberg?
options: Readers see a consistent snapshot of the table
Tables are isolated from each other
questions.correctAnswer: Readers see a consistent snapshot of the table
questions.explanation: Snapshot isolation in Iceberg ensures that readers see a consistent snapshot of the table at a point in time, even while writes are occurring.

questions.question: What is the metadata file in Iceberg?
questions.correctAnswer: Stores schema and table properties
questions.explanation: The metadata file in Iceberg contains the schema, table properties, and partition information.

questions.question: What is a manifest file in Iceberg?
options: Lists data files and their metadata
questions.correctAnswer: Lists data files and their metadata
questions.explanation: A manifest file in Iceberg contains a list of data files with their metadata, such as file location, size, and partition information.

questions.question: What is partition evolution in Iceberg?
options: Changing partition scheme without rewriting data
questions.correctAnswer: Changing partition scheme without rewriting data
questions.explanation: Partition evolution allows you to change the partitioning scheme of an Iceberg table without rewriting all the data.

questions.question: What is view evolution in Iceberg?
questions.correctAnswer: Changing schema without rewriting data
questions.explanation: View evolution in Iceberg allows you to change the schema of a view without rewriting the underlying data.

questions.question: What is hidden partitioning in Iceberg?
options: Partitioning visible to queries but not to users
questions.correctAnswer: Partitioning visible to queries but not to users
questions.explanation: Hidden partitioning in Iceberg allows partitioning data for performance while hiding the partitioning columns from query results.

questions.question: Which company originally developed Hudi?
questions.correctAnswer: Uber
questions.explanation: Apache Hudi was originally developed by Uber for near-real-time data ingestion and processing.

questions.question: What does Hudi stand for?
questions.correctAnswer: Hadoop Upsert Delete Incremental
questions.explanation: Hudi stands for Hadoop Upsert Delete Incremental, reflecting its support for upsert and delete operations on data lakes.

questions.question: What is MOR in Hudi?
questions.correctAnswer: Merge-On-Read table type
questions.explanation: MOR (Merge-On-Read) is a table type in Hudi where updates are stored as delta files and merged during read time.

questions.question: What is COW in Hudi?
questions.correctAnswer: Copy-On-Write table type
questions.explanation: COW (Copy-On-Write) is a table type in Hudi where updates create new file versions and old files are deleted.

questions.question: What is an index in Hudi?
options: Data structure to quickly locate records
questions.correctAnswer: Data structure to quickly locate records
questions.explanation: An index in Hudi is a data structure (like a HBase or bloom filter index) that allows quick location of records for updates and deletes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Landing zone in a data lake?
questions.correctAnswer: Temporary storage for incoming data
questions.explanation: The Landing zone is for temporary storage of incoming raw data before it's validated and moved to the Raw zone.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Raw zone in a data lake?
options: Persistent storage of immutable raw data
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent storage of immutable raw data
questions.explanation: The Raw zone stores immutable raw data in its original format, serving as the single source of truth.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Cleaned zone?
options: Data that has been validated and cleansed
questions.correctAnswer: Data that has been validated and cleansed
questions.explanation: The Cleaned zone contains data that has been validated, cleansed, and standardized from the Raw zone.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Curated zone?
options: Business-ready data with relationships and rules
questions.correctAnswer: Business-ready data with relationships and rules
questions.explanation: The Curated zone contains business-ready data that has been enriched with relationships, business rules, and aggregations.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Consumption zone?
options: Data optimized for end-user access and analytics
questions.correctAnswer: Data optimized for end-user access and analytics
questions.explanation: The Consumption zone contains data that has been optimized for end-user access, analytics, and visualization.

questions.question: What is data governance in a data lake?
options: Policies, procedures, and standards for data management
questions.correctAnswer: Policies, procedures, and standards for data management
questions.explanation: Data governance defines policies, procedures, standards, and metrics that ensure the effective and efficient use of data.

questions.question: What is metadata management in a data lake?
options: Capture, storage, and management of data about data
questions.correctAnswer: Capture, storage, and management of data about data
questions.explanation: Metadata management involves capturing, storing, and managing information about the data (schema, lineage, ownership, etc.).

questions.question: What is data lineage in a data lake?
options: History of data transformations and movements
questions.correctAnswer: History of data transformations and movements
questions.explanation: Data lineage tracks the flow of data from source to destination, including all transformations and movements.

questions.question: What is a data catalog in a data lake?
options: Centralized repository of metadata for data discovery
questions.correctAnswer: Centralized repository of metadata for data discovery
questions.explanation: A data catalog is a centralized repository of metadata that makes data assets discoverable, understandable, and usable.

questions.question: What is data quality management in a data lake?
questions.correctAnswer: Ensuring data meets quality standards
questions.explanation: Data quality management ensures data meets defined quality standards such as accuracy, completeness, consistency, and timeliness.

questions.question: What is data security in a data lake?
options: Protecting data from unauthorized access and breaches
questions.correctAnswer: Protecting data from unauthorized access and breaches
questions.explanation: Data security involves protecting data from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction.

questions.question: What is data retention in a data lake?
options: Policies for how long data should be kept
questions.correctAnswer: Policies for how long data should be kept
questions.explanation: Data retention defines policies for how long different types of data should be kept in the data lake.

questions.question: What is data archiving in a data lake?
options: Moving infrequently accessed data to cheaper storage
questions.correctAnswer: Moving infrequently accessed data to cheaper storage
questions.explanation: Data archiving moves infrequently accessed data from expensive hot storage to cheaper cold storage while maintaining access.

questions.question: What is tiered storage in a data lake?
options: Different storage types based on access frequency
questions.correctAnswer: Different storage types based on access frequency
questions.explanation: Tiered storage uses different storage types (hot, warm, cold) based on data access frequency and performance requirements.

questions.question: What is hot storage in a data lake?
options: Fast, expensive storage for frequently accessed data
questions.correctAnswer: Fast, expensive storage for frequently accessed data
questions.explanation: Hot storage is fast, expensive storage (like SSD) used for frequently accessed data that requires low-latency access.

questions.question: What is cold storage in a data lake?
options: Slow, cheap storage for infrequently accessed data
questions.correctAnswer: Slow, cheap storage for infrequently accessed data
questions.explanation: Cold storage is slow, cheap storage (like HDD or cloud archive) used for infrequently accessed data.

questions.question: What is data partitioning in a data lake?
options: Dividing data into manageable subsets based on criteria
questions.correctAnswer: Dividing data into manageable subsets based on criteria
questions.explanation: Data partitioning divides large datasets into smaller, manageable subsets based on criteria like date, region, or business unit.

questions.question: What is partition pruning in a data lake?
questions.correctAnswer: Skipping irrelevant partitions during queries
questions.explanation: Partition pruning is an optimization that skips reading partitions that don't contain relevant data for a query, improving performance.

questions.question: What is bucketing in a data lake?
questions.correctAnswer: Hash-based partitioning within partitions
questions.explanation: Bucketing uses hash-based partitioning within existing partitions to co-locate related data and improve join performance.

questions.question: What is clustering in a data lake?
options: Co-locating related data in the same files
questions.correctAnswer: Co-locating related data in the same files
questions.explanation: Clustering (like Z-Ordering) co-locates related data in the same files to minimize I/O during queries.

questions.question: What is compaction in a data lake?
options: Combining small files into larger ones
questions.correctAnswer: Combining small files into larger ones
questions.explanation: Compaction combines many small files into larger files to improve query performance by reducing the number of files to read.

questions.question: What is the small file problem in data lakes?
options: Too many small files causing performance issues
Small files are hard to store
Small files are hard to process
questions.correctAnswer: Too many small files causing performance issues
questions.explanation: The small file problem occurs when there are too many small files, which causes performance issues due to high metadata overhead and many I/O operations.

questions.question: What is data compression in a data lake?
options: Reducing data size to save storage and improve performance
questions.correctAnswer: Reducing data size to save storage and improve performance
questions.explanation: Data compression reduces the size of data files to save storage space and improve I/O performance by reading less data.

questions.question: What is columnar storage in a data lake?
options: Storing data by columns instead of rows
questions.correctAnswer: Storing data by columns instead of rows
questions.explanation: Columnar storage stores data by columns instead of rows, which is more efficient for analytical queries that typically read only a subset of columns.

questions.question: What is Parquet format?
options: Columnar storage format optimized for analytics
questions.correctAnswer: Columnar storage format optimized for analytics
questions.explanation: Parquet is an open-source columnar storage file format optimized for use with big data processing frameworks like Spark and Hadoop.

questions.question: What is ORC format?
options: Optimized Row Columnar format for Hadoop
questions.correctAnswer: Optimized Row Columnar format for Hadoop
questions.explanation: ORC (Optimized Row Columnar) is a columnar file format created for Hadoop that provides efficient columnar storage with compression.

questions.question: What is Avro format?
options: Row-based format with schema evolution support
questions.correctAnswer: Row-based format with schema evolution support
questions.explanation: Avro is a row-based binary format that supports schema evolution, making it suitable for data that changes over time.

questions.question: What is the advantage of columnar formats for analytics?
questions.correctAnswer: Efficient reading of specific columns
questions.explanation: Columnar formats allow analytical queries to read only the columns they need, dramatically reducing I/O and improving performance.

questions.question: What is predicate pushdown in a data lake?
options: Filtering data at the storage layer before reading
questions.correctAnswer: Filtering data at the storage layer before reading
questions.explanation: Predicate pushdown pushes filter conditions down to the storage layer, allowing files or partitions to be skipped entirely during reads.

questions.question: What is column pruning in a data lake?
options: Reading only the columns needed for a query
questions.correctAnswer: Reading only the columns needed for a query
questions.explanation: Column pruning is an optimization where only the columns required by a query are read, rather than reading entire files.

questions.question: What is a data lake on AWS?
questions.correctAnswer: S3-based data lake
questions.explanation: On AWS, a data lake is typically built on Amazon S3, with services like AWS Glue for metadata and Athena for querying.

questions.question: What is AWS Glue?
options: Serverless ETL and data catalog service
questions.correctAnswer: Serverless ETL and data catalog service
questions.explanation: AWS Glue is a serverless ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) service that also provides a data catalog for metadata management.

questions.question: What is Athena on AWS?
options: Serverless query service for data in S3
questions.correctAnswer: Serverless query service for data in S3
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service that allows you to analyze data in Amazon S3 using standard SQL.

questions.question: What is Azure Data Lake Storage?
options: Scalable cloud storage for big data analytics
questions.correctAnswer: Scalable cloud storage for big data analytics
questions.explanation: Azure Data Lake Storage is a scalable cloud storage service optimized for big data analytics workloads.

questions.question: What is Google Cloud Storage for data lakes?
options: Object storage service for data lakes
questions.correctAnswer: Object storage service for data lakes
questions.explanation: Google Cloud Storage is an object storage service that can be used as the foundation for a data lake on Google Cloud.

questions.question: What is BigQuery for data lakes?
options: Serverless data warehouse with data lake capabilities
questions.correctAnswer: Serverless data warehouse with data lake capabilities
questions.explanation: Google BigQuery is a serverless data warehouse that can query data directly from Cloud Storage, providing data lake capabilities.

questions.question: What is Databricks Lakehouse?
options: Unified data lake and warehouse platform
questions.correctAnswer: Unified data lake and warehouse platform
questions.explanation: Databricks Lakehouse Platform provides a unified architecture that combines the best of data lakes and data warehouses.

questions.question: What is Auto Loader in Databricks?
questions.correctAnswer: Incremental file ingestion service
questions.explanation: Auto Loader is a Databricks service that incrementally ingests new files as they arrive in cloud storage.

questions.question: What is Photon in Databricks?
options: Vectorized query engine for faster SQL
questions.correctAnswer: Vectorized query engine for faster SQL
questions.explanation: Photon is Databricks' vectorized query engine that provides significant performance improvements for SQL workloads.

questions.question: What is Unity Catalog in Databricks?
options: Centralized governance solution for data and AI assets
questions.correctAnswer: Centralized governance solution for data and AI assets
questions.explanation: Unity Catalog is Databricks' centralized governance solution for managing data, files, tables, ML models, and dashboards.

questions.question: What is data sharing in Databricks?
questions.correctAnswer: Securely sharing data between organizations
questions.explanation: Databricks Delta Sharing allows organizations to securely share data with other organizations without copying or moving the data.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a bronze table in Databricks medallion architecture?
questions.correctAnswer: Raw data with minimal transformations
questions.explanation: In Databricks' medallion architecture, bronze tables contain raw data from source systems with minimal transformations.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a silver table in Databricks medallion architecture?
questions.correctAnswer: Cleaned, validated, and enriched data
questions.explanation: Silver tables in the medallion architecture contain cleaned, validated, and enriched data that addresses data quality issues.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a gold table in Databricks medallion architecture?
options: Business-ready data for analytics and ML
questions.correctAnswer: Business-ready data for analytics and ML
questions.explanation: Gold tables contain business-ready data that has been aggregated, joined, and prepared for analytics, reporting, and machine learning.

questions.question: What is CDF in Delta Lake?
options: Continuous Data Feed for change data capture
questions.correctAnswer: Continuous Data Feed for change data capture
questions.explanation: CDF (Continuous Data Feed) is a feature in Delta Lake that enables change data capture, tracking row-level changes in tables.

questions.question: What is Dynamic File Pruning in Delta Lake?
options: Skipping files that don't match query predicates
questions.correctAnswer: Skipping files that don't match query predicates
questions.explanation: Dynamic File Pruning uses statistics stored in the transaction log to skip files that don't match query predicates, improving performance.

questions.question: What is Dynamic Partition Pruning in Delta Lake?
options: Skipping partitions that don't match query predicates
questions.correctAnswer: Skipping partitions that don't match query predicates
questions.explanation: Dynamic Partition Pruning skips entire partitions that don't match query predicates, providing significant performance improvements.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a data mesh?
options: Decentralized data architecture with domain ownership
questions.correctAnswer: Decentralized data architecture with domain ownership
questions.explanation: Data mesh is a decentralized data architecture that treats data as a product, with domain ownership and self-serve data infrastructure.

questions.question: What is domain ownership in data mesh?
options: Business domains own their data products
questions.correctAnswer: Business domains own their data products
questions.explanation: In data mesh, business domains (like Finance, Marketing) own their data products, ensuring quality and relevance.

questions.question: What is a data product in data mesh?
questions.correctAnswer: Self-contained, reusable data asset
questions.explanation: A data product in data mesh is a self-contained, reusable data asset that is managed as a product with defined interfaces and SLAs.

questions.question: What is self-serve data infrastructure in data mesh?
options: Platform that enables domain teams to serve their data
questions.correctAnswer: Platform that enables domain teams to serve their data
questions.explanation: Self-serve data infrastructure is a platform that enables domain teams to easily publish, discover, and consume data products without central IT involvement.

questions.question: What is federated computational governance in data mesh?
options: Global governance with local domain control
questions.correctAnswer: Global governance with local domain control
questions.explanation: Federated computational governance balances global standards and policies with local domain control and decision-making.
